summary: Feed s112_double is degraded: 9.5% of frames exceed IDS 1518-byte MTU and are dropped by NIC, and 70.7% of traffic remains GRE-encapsulated hiding inner payload from IDS inspection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding jumbo frames (up to 8096 bytes) from jumbo-enabled segments without MTU normalization to a 1Gbps IDS port limited to 1518 bytes. 240/2529 frames (9.5%) exceed threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC silently drops oversize frames, causing 9.5% traffic loss. IDS with needs_full_payload=true loses flow reassembly and signature matching, creating detection blind spots for large-payload attacks.

recommended_fix.why: Normalize MTU on broker to 1518B (fragment, truncate with awareness, or enable jumbo on IDS) so IDS can receive and inspect frames instead of NIC dropping them.

findings.root_cause: 1788/2529 frames (70.7%) arrive still encapsulated in GRE. Broker is mirroring/aggregating tunnel transit without decapsulation/stripping, forwarding outer headers only.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS sees only outer GRE/IP headers, not inner IP/TCP payload. With needs_full_payload=true, IDS signatures, anomaly detection and session tracking fail for 70% of traffic - effectively blind to tunneled attacks.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to strip GRE and forward inner decapsulated packets so IDS can inspect true payload and apply detection logic.
